# Exercises

## Exercise 1: Scatterplot and correlation

```{r}
ggplot(
  mlb11,
  aes(x = at_bats, y = runs)
) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "At-bats",
    y = "Runs",
    title = "Runs scored and at-bats"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Describe the form, direction, strength, and unusual observations.

> 

Does the relationship look linear enough to summarize with a line?

> 

```{r}
mlb11 |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(runs, at_bats)
  )
```

Interpret the correlation.

>

## Exercise 4: The linear model

```{r}
m1 <- lm(
  runs ~ at_bats,
  data = mlb11
)

summary(m1)
```

Write the fitted regression equation.

> 

Fit a model using `homeruns` to predict `runs`.

```{r}

```

Write the fitted equation and interpret the slope.

> 

Report \(R^2\). Which model accounts for more variation in runs?

## Exercise 5: Prediction and residual

```{r}
ggplot(
  mlb11,
  aes(x = at_bats, y = runs)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Predict runs for a team with 5,579 at-bats:

```{r}
predict(
  m1,
  newdata = data.frame(
    at_bats = 5579
  )
)
```

Find the observed team:

```{r}
mlb11 |>
  filter(at_bats == 5579) |>
  select(team, at_bats, runs)
```

What is the residual? Is the prediction an overestimate or an underestimate?

> 

## Exercise 6: Linearity

```{r}
model_check <- tibble(
  fitted = fitted(m1),
  residual = resid(m1)
)

ggplot(
  model_check,
  aes(x = fitted, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Is there an obvious pattern? What does this suggest about linearity?

> 

## Exercise 7: Nearly normal residuals

```{r}
ggplot(
  model_check,
  aes(x = residual)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 10
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Do the residuals appear reasonably symmetric and approximately normal?

> 

## Exercise 8: Constant variability

Return to the residual-versus-fitted plot.

Does the spread of the residuals stay reasonably similar across the fitted values?
